page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. This x86_64 architecture server features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled at 2 threads per core. It is configured with 16 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations place the single-core CPU performance of the c2d-highcpu-8 in the strong category, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2931.08. Multi-core performance is average, as shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 11737.55 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6523.0. Memory bandwidth is stable, measuring 68.67 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 49.73 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Cryptographic and integer operations are supported by hardware-accelerated instructions including AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, which contribute to a Passmark CPU encryption test score of 9346.41.

While single-threaded tasks perform well, multi-threaded decompression tasks show relative weakness, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scoring in the bottom 25%. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes this instance highly cost-efficient for compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints or local storage. It is suited for tasks such as software compilation, static web serving, lightweight database operations, and small-scale language model inference.
